- Any diagrams or runbooks used for audit/incident purposes.

Can you provide these artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2027-04-27)? If you have an internal packet that maps CAIQ questions to our controls, that would help speed review.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Subject: Draft packet: segmented-egress-v1 / controlplane to tenant notes

Team — attaching the draft artifacts (segmented-egress-v1.pdf, controlplane-to-tenant-egress-matrix.csv, private-dedicated-topology-drawio.xml). Below are the control highlights I will fold into the SIG/CAIQ table: 

1) Control-plane segregation
- Control-plane components (orchestrator API, model registry, autoscaler controller) run in a separate management VPC/namespace with strict peering rules. No tenant workloads run on control-plane subnets.
- Management endpoints exposed only to Redwood-operated NAT egress IPs and PrivateLink endpoints; management ingress is limited to operator subnets and our CI/CD jump hosts (source-IP whitelists).

2) Data plane / tenant compute
- Tenant inference pools are provisioned in customer-dedicated VPCs (Dedicated) or in customer-managed VPCs (Private) with explicit routing. Each tenant VPC has a tenant-specific route table and security groups enforcing L4 deny-by-default.
- Sidecar proxy pattern (Envoy) provides per-pod egress policies; Istio mTLS is enforced for inter-service traffic inside the cluster to prevent lateral movement.

3) Egress controls and enforcement mechanisms
- Default egress posture is deny-all. Allowed destinations are maintained in a centrally-managed egress allowlist service (immutable change process).
- Egress translations: Dedicated uses NAT Gateways in isolated egress subnets under our control; Private uses either customer-managed NAT or PrivateLink for vendor integrations. Both options are logged at the gateway level and forwarded to our SCC (Secure Cloud Collector).
- Host-based blocking: calico network policies + host IPTables denylists on worker nodes for a second layer of enforcement.

4) Authentication and key boundaries
- KMS keys for tenant crypto are customer-scoped where required (Private); control-plane keys are in Redwood KMS with strict IAM roles and key rotation audit. HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise customers upon request.

5) Telemetry & evidence
- Flow logs (VPC flow logs) stored in an immutable bucket with retention metadata; control-plane to tenant NSG changes are auditable (IAM activity + config snapshots).
- We include playbook references: "egress-block-incident-runbook.md" and a traceroute/flow-capture SOP used during investigations.

6) SIG/CAIQ mapping notes (high level)
- CAIQ: Network boundary controls -> VPC peering + PrivateLink diagrams.
- SIG: Network segregation -> mapping to our deny-by-default egress + sidecar enforcement + host-level controls.

Attachments inside the Drive folder; I've also included a small screenshot (egress-scc-screenshot.png) showing our SCC dashboard for egress allowlist changes. Marcus, can you confirm the NAT IP ranges assigned to the Verdant Dedicated pool so we can include them in the matrix?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

  • Runbook: egress-block-incident-runbook.md — Drive/Runbooks/egress-block-incident-runbook.md

- Short answers to your earlier bullets: 
  • "How do you prevent customer data from escaping tenant boundaries?" — Tenant compute never shares host namespaces with other tenants; network policies and sidecar egress filters block unknown destinations; any cross-tenant routing requires explicit peering and is prevented by deny-by-default route tables.
  • "Where are control-plane endpoints located and who can access them?" — Control-plane endpoints sit in a dedicated management VPC and are reachable only via PrivateLink endpoints or our operator subnets. Access is RBAC + source-IP restricted; configuration changes are logged and require 2-person approval for production-impacting rules.

Next steps: Alex, please confirm if you want the CAIQ/Q&A rows pre-filled with our standard references (we can attach a pre-mapped CSV) or if you prefer the annotated PDF + link bundle only.
